niche: a utility power line contractor's 2027 recordable injury forecast for the contract-year safety plan its electric cooperative client's contractor safety standard requires, read once the crews' recognition bonus for every 90 consecutive days without a recordable ends
answer: 255 recordable injuries in 2027, a rate of 3.57 per 200,000 hours on the 2027 work plan's 14,288,000 hours, over the standard's 3.0 (the limit allows 214)
answer_source: generator/analysis.py main(); figures.json forecast_recordables_2027 and forecast_rate_2027
analyst_test: A strong analyst who stacks the two case systems, keeps each case's final classification, drops recurrences and mutual-aid work, joins each recordable to the injured worker's crew on the day, nets paid leave, holiday pay and mutual-aid hours out of the timesheets and reads the recognition notice correctly carries the 2021 to 2026 recorded rate (2.46 per 200,000 hours) onto the 2027 plan and files 176 recordables inside the 3.0 limit, or tests the bonus against the meter and locating technicians it never covered, finds them lower (1.92 against the crews' 2.55), and files the same; the crews record 3.84 in the first 35 days of their counts and about 1.0 in the last 25, and read where the count exerts no pull 2027 makes 255 recordables, 3.57.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is the latent injury rate behind a count that crews thin by choosing not to report as a reward nears, estimated as limited-dependent-variable econometrics estimates a latent rate behind a selected count (each crew's recorded rate where the reward exerts no pull, the reporting choice varying with the reward at stake), carried onto the hours each kind of crew will work; put kilowatt-hours and meters in for injuries and crews and no reading is held back as a meter nears a milestone, so the call has nothing to stand on.
layer1: two incident systems: the legacy EHS log to 31 May 2024 and the case management export after it, with different case numbers, date formats and classification codes, and the cases open at the migration in both
case revisions: a case entered as first aid and revised to medical treatment once the clinic visit is known, restricted work revised to days away
the nurse line's interface opening a first-aid case of its own from each call, dated the day of the call, beside the supervisor's report of the same injury
recurrences opened as cases of their own and linked to the first case
the injured worker's crew read from a dated crew assignment history, workers moving between crews

timesheet hours by pay period with paid leave, holiday pay and mutual-aid hours in their own columns, prior-period adjustments posted in later periods, and in-system storm support on rows of the district the crew worked in
crew codes recoded at the March 2025 reorganisation of two districts
subcontractors' monthly self-reported returns outside the standard's scope

driver: A recorded count is what the units choose to record, and each unit records less as it nears a milestone that pays it for a clean record and records in full again once the milestone is paid or lost, so the record understates the rate the units show when nothing is at stake; when the reward ends the forward rate is each unit's rate in the stretch of its own cycle where hiding gains nothing, which the units the reward never covered cannot give because they do other work at another risk.
driver_concrete: Redbud's line, underground, substation and tree crews earn a recognition award for every 90 consecutive days without a recordable injury, and the programme ends on 31 December 2026; in the 2021 to 2026 record a crew records 3.84 recordables per 200,000 hours in the first 35 days of a count and about 1.0 in its last 25, while the days-away cases no crew can keep off the log come in at much the same rate throughout, so the record's 2.46 understates the rate the crews will record in 2027, which the technicians outside the programme, at 1.92 on lighter work, appear to refute.
stump: A competent solver who reads the client's standard, the recognition notice and the 2027 work plan correctly carries the recorded rate forward, or checks the programme against the technicians it never covered and finds them lower, and files 176 recordables (2.46 per 200,000 hours) and a 2027 plan inside the 3.0 limit; the step that lands it there is reading the record as the injuries, when the crews leave injuries they can hide off the log late in each 90-day count, and read at the 3.84 they record in the first 35 days of their counts, with the technicians at their own 1.92, 2027 makes 255 recordables, a rate of 3.57, and breaches the limit.

differentiation.task170: task170 forecasts a rail operator's ETCS data-entry errors from a per-attempt failure probability that falls with each driver's own attempt count; task130 has no learning curve: every injury is recorded or not by a crew weighing a clean-record reward, and the forward rate is the crew's own rate where the reward is not at stake.
differentiation.task229: task229's checks see a unit's state just before resetting it; task130's record is a choice made by the unit itself, which records less as its reward nears and in full after it is paid or lost.
differentiation.task141: task141 carries end-of-term outcomes at the rate of terms already at their class maximum; task130 has no term or cap: a crew's recorded injuries dip with its position in a rolling 90-day cycle that the record never stores.
differentiation.task151: task151 prices a stepped bonus on a season total by the chances of clearing each step; task130 prices no bonus: the bonus is the cause of the record's shortfall and its end the forward condition.
differentiation.task179: task179 adds the lift of another body's records to each member's own risk; task130 adds nothing from outside: the shortfall is read inside each crew's own cycle.
differentiation.task253: task253 counts schools below a line from noisy small-sample averages; task130 estimates no level below a line: it recovers what a reward kept out of the record.
differentiation.task174: task174 recovers a gain per repetition from sessions whose stopping rule is informative; task130 has no stopping rule: the record is short where the reward is near and whole where it is not.
differentiation.task122: task122 reads a discretionary aid's effect on conflict alerts at like traffic mix minute by minute; task130 has no aid or traffic mix: a crew's recorded injuries are thinned by the crew itself as a clean-record reward nears, and the forward rate is its rate where the reward is not at stake.
differentiation.task133: task133 counts a taken-over loan's months at risk only from its age at the takeover, a left-truncated record of exposure; task130's exposure is complete and every hour is on the timesheets: the shortfall is in the events, which each crew thins itself as its reward nears.
differentiation.task137: task137's arrivals leave no trace because a referrer serves them elsewhere when the service runs out of capacity, and its later architectures add a second body's units the register never holds; task130 has no capacity, referrer or second body: the same crews' own injuries go unrecorded when the crew's clean-record reward is close.
differentiation.task196: task196 recovers unseen events from the overlap of two capture channels whose second is produced by the firm chasing the first; task130 has one channel and no overlap: the unrecorded injuries are read from the rate each crew records where its reward exerts no pull.
differentiation.task180: task180 v4 loses small earthquakes to instrument noise that follows the clock of the day, the same for every station, until new stations remove the masking; task130's thinning is a choice each crew makes under an incentive, its phase is the crew's own rolling 90-day cycle reset by the crew's own reports and payouts, every injury is exposed to it whatever its size, and the trap is the comparison with workers the reward never covered, not a completeness test on a size distribution.
differentiation.task149: task149 forecasts a logistics operator's recordables per 200,000 hours from a rate that rises with each crew's pace against its engineered standards, every injury on the log; task130's injuries come at a steady latent rate and the log is thinned by the crews' own choice not to report as a clean-record award nears, so the forward rate is read where the award exerts no pull, not modelled on how hard the work is.
differentiation.task166: task166 forecasts a software company's new customers from founders who left existing members, linked across billing records; task130 forecasts injuries a reward has kept off a contractor's log, with no arrival process, no linkage of people across organisations and no regional ranking; the surface overlap is the docx and xlsx deliverables and plain forecasting vocabulary.

lineage.driver: The committed set is read off holdings on a future effective date built forward from a past snapshot of filed returns; the forward roll, with a third party's takeovers of scheduled transfers completed on the fixed interval its settled cases show, reproduces both closed controls because every holder enrolled by the snapshot had filed, but the holder population on the effective date also takes in holders enrolled after the snapshot who have not filed yet, whose units are recoverable only by grouping the transfer extract on the buyer, so a unit the roll leaves under the threshold is over it.

lineage.driver: Members of a closed group leave only when a rationed supply reaches them, and the supply is handed out across a wider list in a filed priority order within each size class, so how many remain at a later date is each member's rank inside its class against the cumulative planned supply, and neither a leaving rate nor a survival curve read off history, which both average over whatever list length the past happened to have, gives it.

lineage.driver: A waiting list is split into classes by an attribute the governing rule works out on the day from each member's composition, while the case record keeps that attribute as last assessed; a run-off forecast against a planned supply has to recompute every member's class on each allocation day, because members age across the rule's thresholds and a record assessed years earlier holds the longest-waiting members in classes they have already left.

lineage.driver: A cover whose first window sees only the events reported soon after they occur is priced on a history in which only some units ran the process that produces those quick, cheap reports, while every unit runs it from the window's start; the window's cost is carried almost entirely by the quick events that only the process's units show, so the history pooled across every unit about halves it, and the process's effect read over a full period of development, where it makes the units look cheaper, points the wrong way; the window is costed at each point of its exposure on the experience of the units that already ran the process, one rate for every unit.

lineage.fate: shipped 2026-10-12 at $784,000 (portal pending); the rule 3 audit of 2026-10-15 read it AT_RISK: funding policy 3.4 ("used as recorded ... no development or tail factor ... no distribution is fitted") filed the estimator by eliminating every rival, 3.2 read as a cost-per-FTE-year recipe and the headline wrong answer ($4,854,000) was a contract misreading; reworked in place as the v4 rule 3 rework
lineage.driver: A cover that pays only for events that both occur and are first reported inside its own window is costed from a full period's cost per unit of exposure, when inside a short window only the events reported soon after they occur can count and here those are the cheap ones; the expected cost is the exposure at each point of the window times the cost of past events reported within the time then left, which neither a full period's cost, its prorated share nor the share of events reported within a year at the average cost gives.

lineage.driver: A cover that pays only for events first reported inside its own short window is priced from a history in which the quick-report process began unit by unit on dates spread across the history, so that every common cut of recent years keeps some unit's months before its start, and only each unit's own start, read from its own report delays, prices the window.

A cover that pays only for events first reported inside its own short window is priced as the count of past events that would report in time at the average cost of all past events, when a past event's cost depends on how soon it was reported, and not in one direction: the quickest reports are costly, the next quickest cheap and the late ones carry most of the money; the expected cost is each past event's own cost counted for the exposure from which its own delay still lands it inside the window, which neither the average cost, the average cost of the events reported within a period nor a smooth curve of cost on delay gives.

lineage.driver: A unit's recorded outcome is a judge's mark, and a judge marks a unit more leniently the more often the judge has visited it, so a forecast window in which a redrawn map hands a large share of the units to judges who have never visited them is understated by every unit's own record, by the team's pooled rate and by a model that gives each judge one criterion; the window is read with each judge's criterion at the number of earlier visits the judge will have made to each unit, which the record's covering visits and past reassignments show and a back-test held out on the latest reassignment confirms.

notes: Architecture 6 re-root, 2026-10-31. Every architecture in the lineage is spent (v3 and v4 in actuarial-science-insurance, v5 in psychology-behavioral-science); the new draw moves to economics-econometrics, discrete-choice-limited-dependent-variable-modeling (labour economics: the reporting choice crews make under an incentive pay scheme), under the same forecasting objective. The first card of this draw (human-factors-ergonomics, causal_design, shape 07, utility_or_infrastructure) was redrawn before registration when task122 v3's card reached the tree holding those axes. The organisation family is other: a power line construction and maintenance contractor, which neither owns nor runs the utility. The decisive gap is population (Gap 2, the file is not the thing): the recordable log is what crews chose to record under a reward for a clean record; time (Gap 1) is second, the 2027 window carrying no reward. The strategy is time_semantics: the record has to be read at each crew's position in its own rolling 90-day cycle, a service clock no file stores, estimated from every cycle the crews ran. G12 leads (a crew-day with nothing recorded late in a cycle is partly a non-answer, and the rollup reconciles only while the reward keeps the blanks blank); G13 follows (the decision window has no reward). The shell is drawn with the world: a how-many question and docx, png and xlsx deliverables, unlike v4 (how-much, pptx plus xlsx) and v5 (pdf plus xlsx). Built 2026-11-01: the ask layer re-sited onto the 2026 first-aid cases by district and quarter (the nurse line's cases beside the supervisors' reports) after the careful solver kept the district recordables, hours and awards; the payroll extract dropped, every count running from HR-14 Revision 2's start on 11 January 2021.
